\[
E_k = \alpha + 2\beta \cos\left(\frac{2k\pi}{n}\right), \quad k = 0, 1, \dots, n-1,
\]

where \(n\) is the number of annulene atoms, and \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are constants. For benzene (\(n = 6\)), the six energy levels are:

\[
\begin{align*}
E_0 & = \alpha + 2\beta, \\
E_1 & = \alpha + \beta, \\
E_2 & = \alpha + \beta, \\
E_3 & = \alpha - \beta, \\
E_4 & = \alpha + \beta, \\
E_5 & = \alpha + \beta.
\end{align*}
\]

E_4 & = \alpha + \beta = -11.9 \, \text{eV}, \\
E_5 & = \alpha + \beta = -11.9 \, \text{eV}.
\end{align*}
\]

In a molecule such as benzene, the energy levels are filled from lowest to highest, and the HOMO (highest occupied molecular orbital) is the highest partially filled orbital, while the LUMO (lowest unoccupied molecular orbital) is the next unoccupied orbital.
